besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: Both halves have their own subject and verb, so the AWS comma is required.

besluite.fout: The stacked objects 'die goed die maker' make readers stumble.
besluite.rede: Same meaning (what making the goods cost the maker), and much easier to read on a first pass.

besluite.fout: The contrast with the outward look in the previous sentence is left implicit and reads abruptly.
besluite.rede: 'Maar' only makes the existing contrast clear; no actor, fact or qualifier changes.

besluite.fout: No comma closing the embedded relative clause before the main verb, and no AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses.
besluite.rede: Both commas are standard punctuation and make the sentence easier to read.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses.
besluite.rede: Correct AWS comma; the protected wording 'Die kopers is gewoonlik min' stays intact.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses.
besluite.rede: Correct AWS comma; both protected wordings either side of it stay word for word.
'maak dit swaar' is natural Afrikaans and carries a sense of hardship, so the proposal is a sideways move.
Changing 'is' to 'word' shifts the tense, and 'die werk betaal word' is idiomatic Afrikaans, so the change shifts meaning without fixing a fault.

besluite.fout: 'bo en bo' is not an Afrikaans expression (the fixed form is 'bo en behalwe').
besluite.rede: 'bo-op die prys' is the natural expression and keeps the meaning of extra money on top of the price.

besluite.fout: 'dit' could point to either the organisation or the mark.
besluite.rede: The block is about what the mark does not promise, so naming the mark removes the ambiguity without changing the claim.

besluite.fout: 'so' after 'soveel ... as wat' is redundant and clumsy.
besluite.rede: Dropping the redundant 'so' leaves the meaning exactly the same and reads cleanly.
'die maker behoorlik betaal word' has its own subject and verb, so the comma is correct, and this is a shared glossary definition.

besluite.fout: Dropping 'dat' and keeping main-clause word order is informal for a written definition.
besluite.rede: The proposal is better written Afrikaans, but it changes the word order of a glossary definition, which only the writer may change across lessons.
